title: UtensilMenace
description: You have been tasked with investigating the PC belonging to the CEO of your company. He told you that he created an account for his son on this PC, and that his son downloaded a game. However, the game did not show up when he tried to open it, so he believes that his son may have downloaded malware. Can you unravel this incident?
highlights: Investigate a CEO's PC where their son unknowingly downloaded a fake game that turned out to be malware. Trace the malicious executable's impact through MFT, event logs, and registry to uncover persistence mechanisms including accessibility features abuse, registry run keys, and malicious service creation.

title: WorkFromHome
description: Zero Divine-Unit's Security Operations Center detected a sudden spike of outbound remote-access traffic and privileged log-ons originating from a single Windows 10 workstation in the development network. The timing matched a peculiar internal chat in which a junior developer repeatedly asked a senior colleague for elevated credentials, prompting the SOC to quarantine the host and capture a full forensic image for review. As part of Zero Divine-Unit's DFIR team, you now possess that image, the complete senior-junior chat transcript, and concise IT-meeting notes collected during the response. Your mission is to reconstruct the sequence of events, determine any data or credential exposure, and distill actionable remediation and hardening recommendations for leadership.
highlights: Investigate how an attacker used social engineering and a fake tech support call to trick the victim into installing an RMM tool. Trace the full chain from browser download through remote access, Sticky Keys backdoor, and privilege escalation via SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege.

title: ResourcePacks
description: Manuel, an enthusiastic gamer, recently installed popular Minecraft resource packs on his new computer after classmates shared download links with him. Soon after, he noticed system slowdowns, unexpected pop-ups, and malfunctioning applications. You have been asked to investigate how a suspicious file infiltrated the machine, whether it created hidden persistence mechanisms, and assess any impact on personal data or overall system stability.
highlights: Investigate a FileFix-style attack where a threat actor lured the victim via a fake Minecraft resource pack YouTube video. Trace the full chain from browser history through UAC bypass via ComputerDefaults.exe, WMI persistence, backdoor user creation, and privilege escalation via SeImpersonatePrivilege.

title: YARA Trap
description: Wowza Enterprise recently deployed a secure malware analysis portal on an isolated workstation, accessible only to internal threat analysts. Promoted as part of a critical infrastructure environment, the portal was secretly configured as a honeypot to detect insider threats. Unexpected behaviors were observed on the system, including rule submissions triggering unexplained command activity and the creation of unfamiliar files. Security teams suspect the portal's functionality was exploited to gain deeper access, potentially enabling the attacker to establish persistence and escalate privileges within the isolated environment. Your task is to investigate the forensic artifacts provided to uncover how the attacker gained access, what actions they performed, and whether they established any mechanisms to maintain long-term control over the system.
highlights: Investigate a compromised web server where the attacker exploited a file upload vulnerability, deployed a webshell, established persistence through BITS jobs, and escalated privileges. Analyze MFT, prefetch, registry hives, and IIS logs to reconstruct the full attack timeline.

title: Spooler - APT28
description: The SOC team was notified by the IT department regarding a potentially compromised workstation recently reassigned to a new government employee named Keela. Upon receiving the workstation, Keela reported unusually slow performance and suspected the system had not been properly cleaned before being handed over. The IT team initiated a routine cleanup but identified indicators of suspicious activity suggesting that the machine, and possibly the department's website may have been previously compromised. As a forensics investigator, you have been provided with a disk image of Keela's workstation. Your task is to perform a comprehensive investigation to uncover any signs of malicious activity, reconstruct the timeline of events, and assess the scope and impact of the potential compromise.
highlights: Hunt through browser downloads, MFT records, and Prefetch artifacts to unmask the initial dropper in an APT28-themed scenario. Rebuild the complete attack timeline from initial access through persistence and privilege escalation using Print Spooler exploitation.

title: Perfect Survey
description: The Wowza Sport website recently came under a suspected cyberattack. Internal stakeholders believe that a rival competitor may be behind the incident. On the day of the attack, monitoring systems detected a sudden and abnormal surge in incoming web requests, overwhelming the company's online services. Your task is to investigate the compromised web server, which also functions as the domain controller for the Wowza Sport environment. You are expected to analyze logs, identify the source and method of the attack, and assess the potential impact on both the website and the organization's Active Directory infrastructure.
highlights: Investigate a compromised web server doubling as a domain controller for a sports organization. Use SIEM and log analysis to identify the attack source, method of exploitation, and assess the impact on both the website and Active Directory infrastructure.

title: LFI Escalation
description: IT staff reported unusual behavior on a workstation running a web application, triggered by an antivirus detection of a suspicious file. Early indicators suggest the website may have served as the entry point. Your task is to investigate the full scope of the compromise — tracing how the attacker gained access, what actions they performed, and how they established persistence on the system.
highlights: Trace a full compromise starting from a Local File Inclusion vulnerability on a website through to system-level persistence. Analyze web server logs and endpoint artifacts to map out how the attacker escalated from web access to full system control.

title: KioskExpo7
description: On October 18, 2025, Wowza Enterprise hosted their first-ever cybersecurity conference. To streamline registration, the IT team configured several laptops in Windows Kiosk mode to display a QR-code registration page for attendee self-service. After the event concluded, the security team detected suspicious outbound connections originating from one of the kiosk devices KioskExpo7. Surveillance footage revealed a suspicious individual spending an unusually long time interacting with that particular terminal. You have been provided with a KAPE triage image from the compromised kiosk. Your mission is to reconstruct the complete attack timeline, identify the breakout and escalation techniques used, and assess the full scope and impact of the compromise.
highlights: Investigate a physical kiosk breakout at a conference where the attacker escaped Edge kiosk mode via the Help feature, downloaded tools, escalated to admin via registry-stored credentials, replaced the registration QR code with a phishing link, and set up scheduled task persistence for C2 communication.

title: RoastToRoot
description: After compromising a Linux server within the environment, the threat actor was able to pivot deeper into the network and ultimately gain access to the domain controller. From there, they deployed ransomware across the Wowza Enterprise infrastructure, resulting in widespread system outages and the loss of all recoverable backups. Fortunately, network traffic from the first day of the intrusion, specifically communications between the compromised Linux host and the domain controller, was captured and preserved. Your task is to analyze this evidence to determine how the breach occurred, identify the attacker's actions and access path, and provide clear, actionable lessons learned for the organization to strengthen its security posture and prevent similar incidents in the future.
highlights: Reconstruct a complete Active Directory domain compromise from network traffic. Identify AS-REP Roasting and Kerberoasting attacks, crack service account hashes offline, then trace privilege escalation, lateral movement across the domain, and data exfiltration via rclone.

title: RaaS Unfold - RansomHub
description: The incident response team was tasked by Wowza Unlimited's parent company to investigate the attack. They obtained the hash of the ransomware responsible for encrypting all files. This hash can help determine the ransomware's capabilities and identify its operator. Your job is to find all relevant information related to this ransomware — this is critical for helping leadership decide whether to pay the ransom or alert the authorities.

title: Recruiter - Hanoi Op
description: Wowza Enterprise operates a public job application portal that allows interested candidates to submit their personal information and CVs. The HR team regularly reviews submitted resumes and schedules interviews with suitable candidates. During a routine CV review, Patinthida, an HR specialist at Wowza Enterprise, noticed something unusual. One candidate had submitted their resume as a ZIP archive. Upon extracting and opening the contents, a PDF file was launched from an unexpected and unfamiliar location on the workstation. Alarmed by this behavior, Patinthida immediately shut down her workstation and contacted the IT team for assistance. Your task is to investigate what occurred on this workstation, reconstruct the sequence of events, and determine whether Wowza Enterprise experienced a potential security breach.

title: CodeFreeze
description: Caspery, a senior developer working remotely for Wowza Enterprise, reported that his git commit commands were taking unusually long to complete. Several days later, the Threat Intelligence team discovered Caspery's credentials and API keys leaked on a dark web forum. The data included sensitive information from Wowza's internal systems. The Incident Response plan was immediately activated. A forensic team was dispatched to acquire an image of Caspery's workstation. Your mission is to conduct an analysis on the forensic image to identify the root cause of the breach. Time is critical — the data is already compromised and actively being traded on dark web marketplaces.
highlights: Investigate a developer workstation compromised through a fake auditor's meeting script. Trace how the attacker exploited Backup Operators group membership, hijacked a service DLL for privilege escalation, and planted a malicious Git pre-commit hook to exfiltrate secrets from every code commit.

title: Satisfaction
description: Wowza Innotech hosted an onsite customer meetup at their headquarters. Each session concluded with attendees completing a satisfaction survey on an internal workstation accessible only within the building's network. During one session, a customer noticed the survey page redirected them to a suspicious external site prompting a file download. They reported it immediately to the IT and Incident Response (IR) team. Initial triage confirmed the survey workstation had been compromised. Internal interviews revealed that one attendee had a heated disagreement with staff over product performance — an individual with a history of misusing technology when upset. Given the timing, the IR team suspected the compromise occurred during the meeting itself, likely by someone physically present on the network. Fortunately, the network operations team had been capturing traffic during the event for monitoring purposes. This packet capture was handed over for deeper analysis.
highlights: Investigate a compromised LimeSurvey platform where the attacker brute-forced admin credentials, uploaded a malicious plugin containing a web shell, injected shellcode into explorer.exe for a reverse shell, and modified the survey to redirect users to a drive-by download site.

title: Penumbra
description: Wowza Technology has suffered another breach, and this time security awareness training was not enough to stop it. The victim is Patricia Kyrielight, a document controller responsible for files tied to a classified government project still under development. Because her role gives her broad access to sensitive design and infrastructure documentation, compromising her workstation was enough to expose the inner workings of the project. The incident came to light when an endpoint security alert flagged unauthorized remote-access software running on Patricia's machine, a direct violation of company policy. A closer look revealed far more than a policy breach: the attacker had already established persistence early in the day, then returned hours later for a hands-on session while Patricia was away from her desk. During that session they searched her files, pulled confidential material from her cloud-synced storage, and worked methodically to erase their tracks before disconnecting. You have been handed a triage image of the affected workstation. Reconstruct the intrusion from initial access through exfiltration, account for the attacker's anti-forensic activity, and determine the full extent of what was accessed and taken.

title: CodeFreeze 2
description: The intrusion began with a senior engineer on Wowza Enterprise's development team. As the incident response team worked to contain the compromise, it became clear the attacker's reach had not ended with that single account. Johnny Tronus, a data scientist on the marketing team, used a dedicated virtual machine to process the company's sales data. When news of the breach spread, he recalled a recent email exchange with the compromised engineer and the file he had been persuaded to download from it. Suspecting his own machine might be affected, he escalated to the incident response team without delay. IR moved quickly to contain and triage the VM, captured a full image, and passed it down the chain for investigation. That image is now in your hands. Work through the evidence to reconstruct the attack from start to finish: how the actor first gained access, the actions they took on the host, the mechanisms they used to maintain their foothold, and the sensitive data they ultimately put at risk.

title: WorkFromHome (HTB)
description: Wowza Enterprise (Wowza Inc.) has hired you to investigate an incident involving a workstation used by Otello John, which is believed to have been compromised by a threat actor. The attacker reportedly changed the desktop wallpaper to a questionable image. The IT team has already provided you with initial information, and it is your duty to report back your findings.
highlights: Investigate a compromised workstation where the threat actor phished credentials via a fake SSO page, gained RDP access, exploited SeManageVolumePrivilege to replace a Print Spooler DLL, and established persistence through a hidden VBScript in the Startup folder that loads a malicious DLL via WMI.

title: Liberty
description: Liberty launched a massive project with a budget exceeding $100 million, with the goal of granting true freedom to humanity One day, a system administrator discovered a shared folder configured with “Full Control” permissions granted to “Everyone”, raising concerns about a potential security incident. You have been tasked with investigating evidence collected from the affected endpoint to determine what occurred. Threat Intelligence has previously identified that an employee’s credentials were harvested by a RedLine Stealer, which is suspected to have been used for initial access to this system.
highlights: Investigate a compromised endpoint where stolen credentials from a RedLine Stealer were used for initial access. Trace how the attacker exploited an overly permissive shared folder, moved laterally, and escalated privileges across the network.

title: JobApplicant
description: Wowza Grand College has opened a job application portal by creating a website for applicants to upload their resumes for HR to review. Recently, the SOC team observed suspicious enrollments to a certificate template in their ADCS infrastructure. The team began collecting evidence from the compromised domain controller to investigate the cause of the unauthorized certificate enrollments.

title: SHAW
description: Investigating ClickFix incident by correlating Browser history, PowerShell Script Block Logging, Prefetch and PowerShell log together
highlights: Investigate a ClickFix incident by correlating browser history with PowerShell Script Block Logging, Prefetch execution records, and system logs to reconstruct how the victim was tricked into running a malicious command.

title: Master Investigator
description: Investigating incident starting from phishing, privilege escalation to domain compromise with Active Directory Certificate Services.
highlights: Investigate a full attack chain from initial phishing through privilege escalation to domain compromise via Active Directory Certificate Services (ADCS). Correlate browser history, event logs, file system artifacts, and certificate enrollment records to reconstruct the complete intrusion.

title: HotDog
description: Reconstruct an Active Directory intrusion from a single packet capture: recover the Kerberoasted service tickets off the wire, crack both service account hashes offline, then use the derived key material to decrypt the attacker's GSS-API protected LDAP queries and encrypted SMB3 transfers.
highlights: Reconstruct an Active Directory intrusion from a single packet capture by recovering Kerberoasted service tickets, cracking both service account hashes offline, and using the derived key material to decrypt GSS-API protected LDAP queries and encrypted SMB3 file transfers.

title: AS a REPresentative!
description: Reconstruct an Active Directory intrusion from a single packet capture: extract an AS-REP Roastable hash from the Kerberos exchange, crack it offline to recover the account's credentials, then derive the session key material needed to decrypt the attacker's encrypted SMB3 traffic and expose what was actually transferred.
highlights: Extract an AS-REP Roastable hash from a Kerberos exchange in a packet capture, crack it offline to recover account credentials, then derive session key material to decrypt the attacker's encrypted SMB3 traffic and expose the transferred data.

title: You Know The Rules
description: A .NET binary obfuscated with ConfuserEx and then packed with MPRESS. Peel both layers off to reach the managed code, work out why it kills and relaunches Edge on a hardcoded YouTube link, and rebuild the flag from the video title it was so desperate to play.
highlights: Reverse engineer a .NET binary obfuscated with ConfuserEx and packed with MPRESS. Peel both protection layers to reach the managed code, understand why it kills and relaunches Edge on a hardcoded YouTube link, and reconstruct the flag from the video title.

title: The Weakest Link
description: Break a portal's HTTPS three different ways from a single packet capture: read the session negotiated with a NULL cipher suite in the clear, factor a 512-bit RSA certificate to rebuild the server's private key, and recover the (Pre)-Master-Secret leaked over a plaintext HTTP debug channel.
highlights: Break a portal's HTTPS three different ways from a single packet capture: read a session negotiated with a NULL cipher suite, factor a 512-bit RSA certificate to rebuild the server's private key, and recover the (Pre)-Master-Secret leaked over a plaintext HTTP debug channel.

title: Phantom Packets
description: Reconstruct a server compromise from one capture: reassemble an RSA private key smuggled out through DNS AAAA records, use it to decrypt the attacker's TLS session, then carve the Git smart-HTTP packfile out of the cloned repository and rebuild the repo to reach what was hidden in its non-default branches.
highlights: Reconstruct a server compromise from a single capture: reassemble an RSA private key smuggled out through DNS AAAA records, use it to decrypt the attacker's TLS session, then carve a Git smart-HTTP packfile and rebuild the repository to find secrets hidden in non-default branches.

title: Shadow Council
description: Work a KAPE triage image seized from a ransomware operator: pull the saved Windows password out of a Zen browser credential store, unlock the DPAPI master key with it, peel the three encryption layers off Signal Desktop's SQLCipher database, and read the ransom ledger out of the decrypted messages.
highlights: Work a KAPE triage image from a ransomware operator: extract a saved Windows password from a Zen browser credential store, unlock the DPAPI master key, peel three encryption layers off Signal Desktop's SQLCipher database, and read the ransom negotiation ledger from decrypted messages.

title: Awesome Splunk and Elastic SIEM Practice Labs
description: A list of labs with Splunk and Elastic from various CyberSecurity Training platforms such as CyberDefenders, BlueTeamLabs Online (BTLO), TryHackMe, DFIR Labs, Xintra, Ace Responder, and more

title: Awesome Cloud Investigation Labs
description: A list of cloud investigations (Azure, AWS and GCP) from various cybersecurity platforms such as Blue Team Labs Online (BTLO), CyberDefenders, HackTheBox Sherlocks (HTB), CyberWarFare Labs Infinity (CWL Infinity) and so on

title: Pulse Log Generator
description: A blue team training tool that generates realistic, scenario-based server logs for SOC analysts, DFIR students, and CTF challenge authors. Produce authentic attack logs across six log formats with configurable difficulty levels and built-in answer keys.

title: Design your first Windows Forensics Lab and make it decent!
description: A blog about making your very own Windows Forensics lab, not deep dive too much into technical aspect but flavors of Windows Forensics scenarios

title: Using Git Commits as a Persistence Mechanism
description: Research about how red teamer and threat actor can use git history to hide their payload and execute it with the help of other persistence mechanism

title: RMM Forensics Cheat Sheet
description: A repository contains forensic artifacts and indicators for Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools commonly observed in threat actor operations. These cheat sheets are compiled from hands-on research in controlled lab environments to support defensive security operations.

title: RMM & Remote-Access Forensics Research
description: Deep dives into how remote monitoring and management tools behave on Windows and what they leave behind — install and persistence artifacts, connection and file transfer evidence, and what survives an uninstall.

title: BAM Records Process Termination Time, Not Just Execution
description: Registry-level proof that the Background Activity Moderator timestamp marks when a process exited, and how to lean on it when process termination events are unavailable.

title: Browser Download Forensics Research
description: What Chromium download history actually records when a transfer is marked interrupted, and where the stored reason disagrees with what ended up on disk.

title: RustDesk Decryptor
description: A forensic tool for decrypting RustDesk configuration files. Designed for security research, penetration testing, and digital forensics investigations.

title: ResidentReaper
description: A fast NTFS forensic tool written in Rust — parses $MFT and $J (USN Journal) artifacts, and hunts for resident data hidden inside MFT entries.

title: CyberChef Playground
description: A self-hosted CTF-style challenge platform for learning cryptography, encoding, and log analysis — powered by CyberChef recipes.

title: SysTrace
description: A fast, native GUI forensic analysis tool for Sysmon logs. Opens raw .evtx files, EVTXECmd NDJSON exports, or EVTXECmd CSV exports and presents them as an interactive process tree with process-centric telemetry browsing — built for DFIR investigators.

title: TrailInspector
description: A fast, offline desktop tool for investigating AWS CloudTrail logs — built for blue teamers, incident responders, and cloud security engineers.

title: QuotaWatch
description: Multi-provider AI token and quota monitor for Windows (system tray + popup UI) and Linux (statusline + TUI). Tracks Claude, OpenAI Codex, Windsurf, and Google Antigravity with real-time polling, severity alerts, and global hotkeys.
